title: Settings
database.title: Database
database.envNote: Connection settings live in .env and are never shown or editable here.
database.onlyOneTarget: Only one target is configured, so there is nothing to switch between.
database.confirmSwitchContent: The server restarts to connect to the new target. This page will reconnect and reload automatically once it is back. Under `npm run dev`, you may need to restart it by hand.
database.reconnectingSubtitle: Waiting for the server to come back up.
backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.description: A full-fidelity snapshot of every table: every field, every relation, driver-agnostic. Not the same as the CSV/Excel export elsewhere in the app, which is a lossy report meant for people to read. On its own the file is only scrambled (gzip + obfuscation), which is not encryption. Set up encryption under Automatic backups below, and exported files are encrypted too.
backup.dropzone: Click or drag a JobTrack backup file (.jtbak or .jtbak.age) here
backup.previewInfo: Backup taken {{date}}. Restoring will replace everything currently in the active database with:
backup.confirmTitle: Replace all data in the active database?
backup.confirmContent: Every table is wiped and recreated from this backup. This cannot be undone.
backup.encryptedHint: Enter its passphrase, or paste or load the secret key it was encrypted to (AGE-SECRET-KEY-…).
backup.hardwareKeyHint: Encrypted to a YubiKey or another hardware key? Decrypt it first with the age tool, for example: age -d -i yubikey-identity.txt -o backup.jtbak file.jtbak.age, then restore backup.jtbak here.
autoBackup.title: Automatic backups
autoBackup.description: Back up on a schedule to any folder: a OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud folder is uploaded by its sync app, and a network share works too. These settings are kept on this computer, not in the database, so restoring a backup never changes them.
autoBackup.destination.heading: Folder
autoBackup.destination.hint: A full path on the computer running JobTrack. Network shares such as \\server\backups work too.
autoBackup.schedule.heading: Schedule
autoBackup.schedule.skipUnchanged: Skip when nothing has changed since the last backup
autoBackup.schedule.catchUp: A backup missed while the computer was off runs soon after JobTrack starts again.
autoBackup.retention.heading: Keep
autoBackup.retention.keepLast: Keep at most this many backups:
autoBackup.retention.note: The newest backup is always kept. Only files JobTrack wrote for this database are ever deleted.
autoBackup.encryption.heading: Encryption
autoBackup.encryption.noneNote: Backups are only scrambled, not encrypted. Anyone with access to the folder can read them.
autoBackup.passphrase.note: Scheduled backups need the passphrase, so it is saved on this computer. It protects the copies in the cloud or on the network, not this computer. Keys are safer: then nothing on this computer can decrypt the backups.
autoBackup.keys.note: Backups are encrypted with age to every key listed here, and any one of them can decrypt it. JobTrack keeps only the public keys.
autoBackup.keys.addSecond: Add a second key, for example a key kept on paper, so that losing one key does not lose your backups.
autoBackup.keys.duplicate: That key is already in the list
autoBackup.keys.problem.secretKey: This is a secret key. Add its public key (age1…) instead. A secret key is never stored here.
autoBackup.keys.problem.notAgeKey: This is not an age key. Public keys start with age1.
autoBackup.keys.problem.invalid: This key is incomplete or mistyped. Copy it again from where it was created.
autoBackup.keysHelp.title: How backup keys work
autoBackup.keysHelp.anyOneTitle: Any one key opens a backup
autoBackup.keysHelp.anyOne: Each backup is encrypted once, and the code that unlocks it is sealed separately for every key in the list. Any single key can open the backup on its own; you never need all of them.
autoBackup.keysHelp.whySecond: If your only key is lost, for example a YubiKey that breaks or a key file that gets deleted, the backups encrypted to it can never be opened again. Nobody can recover them, including JobTrack. A second key kept somewhere else is your spare.
autoBackup.keysHelp.goodPair: A YubiKey you use day to day, plus a generated key that is printed on paper or saved in a password manager and kept away from this computer.
autoBackup.keysHelp.changes: Changes apply to new backups only. Backups already written can still be opened only by the keys they were made with, so keep an old key until retention has deleted the backups made with it.
autoBackup.keysHelp.publicOnly: Only the public keys (age1…). They can lock backups but not open them, so nothing on this computer can read the backups it writes.
autoBackup.keysHelp.docsLink: Read more in the JobTrack documentation
autoBackup.keys.hardwareHint: Hardware keys: install age-plugin-yubikey (or another age plugin such as age-plugin-fido2-hmac or age-plugin-tpm), set up the key with it, and add the age1yubikey1… key it prints. The key only needs to be plugged in to restore.
autoBackup.keys.secretWarning: Save this secret key somewhere safe, away from this computer: a password manager, or printed on paper. It is shown only now. Without it, backups made with this key cannot be restored.
autoBackup.keys.confirmSaved: I have saved the secret key
autoBackup.saveError: Could not save the backup settings
autoBackup.testOk: Everything checks out: the folder is writable and every key works.
autoBackup.files.error: Could not read the backup folder
autoBackup.files.empty: No backups in this folder yet

data.title: Reset & demo data
data.description: Wipe everything in the active database, or (only while it's empty) fill it with a realistic multi-year demo dataset to explore the app with.
data.clearWarning: This permanently deletes every row below. There is no undo. Export a backup first if you might want this data again.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.description: What you are looking for. The Openings page ranks saved openings against it and shows why each one scored as it did. Leave anything blank that does not matter to you.

profile.aboutYou.tooltip: Compared with each posting by meaning, once the search model has loaded. A pasted CV works well.
profile.aboutYou.placeholder: Backend engineer, eight years in payments and data platforms. Kotlin, Postgres, Kafka.
profile.targetTitles.label: Job titles you want
profile.locationTiers.label: Places you would work, by priority
profile.locationTiers.tooltip: Put places that matter equally in the same level. A posting earns the level's share of the location points; the highest level it matches counts. Drag places between levels, and levels by their handle.
profile.locationTiers.shareLabel: Share of the location points at priority {{level}}
profile.locationTiers.shareTooltip: Share of the location points a posting here earns
profile.locationTiers.alreadyIn: {{place}} is already in priority {{level}}. Drag it to move it.

profile.locationTiers.newLevelDrop: Drop a place here to start a new priority level
profile.locationTiers.unrankedHint: Not ranked. Drag a place into a level to rank it, or drop one here to unrank it.
profile.locationTiers.unrankedEmpty: Every known place is ranked. Drop a place here to unrank it.
profile.workModes.label: Work modes
profile.workModes.tooltip: A remote role counts as in every location when you pick Remote
profile.salaryFloor.label: Lowest salary you would take
profile.salaryCurrency.label: Currency
profile.includeKeywords.label: Words that make a posting better
profile.excludeKeywords.label: Words that rule a posting out
profile.excludeKeywords.tooltip: Each one found takes a large share off the score

sources.platforms.title: Job platforms
sources.platforms.description: The job boards and sites you search, most important first. An assistant connected to JobTrack reads this list to know where to look and in what order.
sources.apis.title: Job APIs
sources.apis.description: Job APIs an assistant can query for you, most important first, such as JobTech Jobsearch for every ad in Platsbanken. JobTrack does not call these itself.

locations.title: Known locations
locations.description: The places offered when you type a location into your profile. Places you rank are added here on their own. Rename one to fix its spelling everywhere, or remove one you do not want offered.
locations.removeRanked: It is also taken out of priority {{level}} in your profile.
automation.title: Automation
automation.followUp.toggleLabel: Give new applications a follow-up date
automation.followUp.note: Only when you leave the date blank, and never a date that has already passed, so importing old applications does not flood your follow-ups.
automation.ghost.note: Applies to applications still at Applied or Screening where nothing has happened in that long: no status change, and no follow-up date in that time. A follow-up planned for later keeps an application safe. It runs every hour while JobTrack is running. Each change is written to the application's status history with a note saying why, so it is easy to undo.
automation.ghost.none: Nothing would be marked ghosted right now.
automation.ghost.candidates_one: {{count}} application would be marked ghosted on the next run
automation.ghost.candidates_other: {{count}} applications would be marked ghosted on the next run
fitWeights.title: Fit scoring
fitWeights.description: How the 0-100 fit score on the Openings page divides its points, and how strict the summary comparison is. Most people never need to change this; it exists for when the default balance does not match what actually matters to you.
fitWeights.pointsHeading: Points out of 100 for each match
fitWeights.fields.title: Title match
fitWeights.excludedPenalty.label: Points lost per excluded keyword
fitWeights.excludedPenalty.tooltip: Taken off the earned share for each excluded keyword found in the posting
fitWeights.semanticFloor.label: Summary similarity floor
fitWeights.semanticFloor.tooltip: Cosine similarity at or below this earns nothing from the summary comparison
fitWeights.semanticCeiling.label: Summary similarity ceiling
fitWeights.semanticCeiling.tooltip: Cosine similarity at or above this earns full marks from the summary comparison
fitWeights.saveSuccess: Fit weights saved. Saved openings are rescored the next time you view them.

remember.description: Pages keep how you left them when you come back. This is stored in this browser only, not in the database, so another browser or computer keeps its own.
remember.groups.view.label: Sorting and layout
remember.groups.view.covers: Sort order, rows per page, the chart grouping on Statistics and the tab under Needs attention.
